---
title: "Information Decay"
description: "Information decay refers to the gradual loss of shared understanding and trust in facts due to ongoing exposure to conflicting narratives and diminished institutional credibility, leading to fragmented communities unable to reach a common consensus."
categories: ["Spillover"]
---


::: {.protected-content}

::: {.function-badge}
[Spillover](../function/spillover.qmd)
:::

The cumulative erosion of shared epistemic foundations through persistent exposure to contradictory narratives, fabricated evidence, and undermined institutional credibility. Over time, populations lose confidence not only in specific claims but in the possibility of establishing shared facts. This degradation is not achieved through any single deception but through the compounding effect of repeated epistemological assaults that fragment consensus reality into incompatible interpretive communities incapable of collective sensemaking.

:::
